Margins expand on lower input cost

Tata Power Company Limited generates and supplies electricity. It  constructs and operates independent power plants, as well as specialises in  transmission and distribution of electricity.   • In Q1FY24, consolidated revenue increased 5.0% YoY to Rs. 15,213cr,  supported by moderate growth in the transmission and distribution  business.  • EBITDA margin rose 850 bps YoY to 21.1%, driven by a decrease in  prices of solar cells, modules and wafers. As a result, reported PAT grew  22.4% YoY to Rs. 973cr.  • Capacity expansions, improvement in execution capabilities, and  corrections in input prices make the business prospects for the  company look promising. Hence, we expect margin improvement to  continue, and upgrade our rating on the stock to BUY with a revised  target price of Rs. 301 based on SOTP valuation.

Moderate growth in revenue   Consolidated revenue grew 5.0% YoY to Rs. 15,213cr in Q1FY24, led by growth of 3.6%  YoY in the transmission and distribution business. The Odisha business stabilised on  the back of various restoration and field activities to overcome uncertain weather  conditions.  The generation business grew a significant 67.5% on a QoQ basis due to  improved cost control and better efficiency. The Mundra plant aided performance  during the quarter and will continue to operate until 30 September 2023. Its  operations may be extended due to heat conditions. In the electric vehicle (EV)  business, the company added 4,400 public chargers and 50,000 home chargers and  plans to add about 1,200 bus chargers across various cities.
*over or under performance to benchmark index

Strong improvement in margins  EBITDA surged 76.0% YoY to Rs. 3,215cr in Q1FY24 on account of a drastic reduction  in prices of solar cells, modules and wafers. Hence, EBITDA margin expanded 850 bps  YoY to 21.1%. Consolidated PAT grew 22.4% YoY to Rs. 973cr, supported by income  from exceptional items (Rs. 235cr).

• In Q1FY24, a capacity addition of 5.8 GW brought the total installed capacity to  ~422GW, of which 77% was attributable to renewable energy.  • The company signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Maharashtra  government of Rs. 13,000cr for pumped hydro storage projects. This project will  support green energy landscape and generate employment for over 6,000 people.  • Tata Power Renewable Energy Limited signed power purchase agreements for  commissioning two solar projects (200MW and 150MW) to provide clean and  sustainable electricity to MSEDCL.

Valuation  Owing to extreme weather conditions in the country, consumption of power was lower  than expected in the quarter. However, the company recorded healthy performance on  account of lower input costs. Capacity additions in the renewable energy segment,  corrections in polysilicon and thermal coal prices, strong execution of business, and  large capex will aid the company in achieving robust operational and financial  performance. Thus, we upgrade our rating on the stock to BUY with a revised target  price of Rs. 301 based on SOTP valuation.
